questions.q_en: Which of the following is the correct order of basicity?
questions.solution_en:
1) Definition of Basicity:

o Basicity refers to the strength of a base, which depends on its ability to donate hydroxide ions (OH−OH^-OH−) in an aqueous solution.

2) Trend in Alkali Metal Hydroxides:

o As we move down Group 1 of the periodic table, the hydroxides of alkali metals become stronger bases due to increased ionic size and solubility in water.

o Order of basicity: CsOH > KOH > NaOH > LiOH.

Explanation of Incorrect Options:

· Option 1, 2, and 3 list incorrect trends that do not align with the periodic properties of alkali metals.

questions.q_en: Which of the following elements is a metalloid?
questions.solution_en: Silicon is classified as a metalloid because it has properties of both metals and non-metals.
questions.solution_hi: Silicon is classified as a metalloid because it has properties of both metals and non-metals.

questions.q_en: Where is sodium located on the periodic table?
questions.solution_en:
The metals are to the left of the line (except for hydrogen, which is a nonmetal), the nonmetals are to the right of the line, and the elements immediately adjacent to the line are the metalloids.

Sodium in the Periodic Table. Sodium, atomic symbol Na, has an atomic number of eleven, and lies in group 1 on the periodic table, below lithium and to the left of magnesium.

questions.q_en: The reaction of an acid and a metal gives:
options_en: Carbon dioxide, salt and hydrogen gas
questions.solution_en:
· When an acid reacts with a metal, the products are salt and hydrogen gas.

· General reaction:

Metal + Acid → Salt + Hydrogen gas

Example: Zn + HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂↑

questions.q_en: Which element of group 13 is a soft metal with a low melting point (303K) and is widely used in doping semiconductors and producing solid-state devices such as transistors?
questions.solution_en:
Gallium, a soft metal of group 13, has the second lowest melting point (after mercury) and can remain in the liquid phase at a larger range of temperatures than any other substance.

With a low melting point of 303K, it is widely used in doping semiconductors and producing solid-state devices such as transistors.

questions.q_en: Which of the following types of elements is included in the leftmost group of the periodic table?
questions.solution_en: The group of elements that are on the far left of the periodic table are called the alkali metals, which have one electron in their outermost shell that they tend to lose easily.

questions.q_en: Which of the following is NOT a halogen gas?
questions.solution_en:
· Halogens are a group of elements in Group 17 of the periodic table, including Fluorine (F), Chlorine (Cl), Bromine (Br), Iodine (I), and Astatine (At).

· Helium (He) is not a halogen; it is a noble gas from Group 18, known for its stability and non-reactivity.
